cd /private/var/folders/kp/vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn/T/barcode-kdo0reo5; cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-var-folders-kp-vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn-T-barcode-kdo0reo5/3576f510-b0f5-4b8c-be13-343cc339e464/scratchpad/c.py <<'EOF'
import subprocess,numpy as np
from PIL import Image
b=np.array(Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')).astype(float)[100]
N=100
def rs(a,n): 
    idx=np.linspace(0,len(a)-1,n).astype(int); return a[idx]
B=rs(b,N)
for L in 'ABCDEFGHIJ':
    out=subprocess.run(['ffmpeg','-v','quiet','-i',f'videos/{L}.mp4','-vf','scale=1:1,fps=1','-f','rawvideo','-pix_fmt','rgb24','-'],capture_output=True).stdout
    v=np.frombuffer(out,np.uint8).reshape(-1,3).astype(float)
    print(L,len(v),np.abs(rs(v,N)-B).mean())
EOF

content.text:
I compared the barcode with the colours of each candidate video. Using ffmpeg, I took one frame per second from every file in `videos/` and shrank each frame to its average colour. I then resampled both the barcode and each video's colour sequence to 100 points and measured the average colour difference between them.

| Option | Mean colour difference (lower is closer) |
|---|---|
| **E. Con Calma** | **12.9** |
| I. Chantaje | 34.3 |
| J. Mayores | 39.7 |
| B. Despacito | 42.2 |
| H. Bum Bum Tam Tam | 42.2 |
| G. Sin Pijama | 43.4 |
| A. Taki Taki | 44.2 |
| F. Waka Waka | 49.5 |
| D. Wheels on the Bus | 71.4 |
| C. Dame Tu Cosita | 99.1 |

Con Calma is far closer than any other option, with less than half the difference of the runner-up. Its colours follow the barcode's pattern: blue scenes first, then reddish-pink ones, then black at the end.

Answer: E
